newsitem.title: UK: Analysts cool on Ockham refinance package.
newsitem.headline: Analysts cool on Ockham refinance package.

text.p: The refinancing package announced by Lloyd's Insurance group Ockham Holdings on Wednesday has left prospective shareholders asking what happens next, analysts said.

Ockham earlier unveiled a 19.5 million-pound price tag for the sale of its aviation and non-marine underwriting operations to Bermudian catastrophe insurer Ace, and announced that U.S. investors led by the Questor group were funding 21 million of a 25 million pound injection into Ockham's motor insurance business, which operates under the name Highway.

"At the moment there are two problems - we don't know exactly how much many there will be left once everything is stripped out, and we don't know what they are going to do with that money," said one leading insurance analyst.

Ockham intends to pump the Questor money into the non-standard motor underwriting business which chief executive Lord David Poole called "very profitable and very exciting." But the analyst was sceptical about how much the portfolio could be increased. He added that it was unclear what the rest of the money would be used for.

His views were echoed by Roman Cizdyn, insurance analyst at Merrill Lynch, who said: "We've had all these announcements before - the only new thing is the figure. They seem to have got a reasonable price from Ace, and the new cash injection appears on reasonable terms."

"But when you look Ockham you've got a 55 percent shareholding of a motor insurance operation and 65 percent of its stockbroking arm Wise Speke, which it plans to float. But the only hint at what else it will go into is that it might be in the financial sector," he said.
He said there was no shareholder nervousness regarding the old liabilities which the group, formerly known as Sturge, incurred during the years when Lloyd's was ravaged by losses.
"These have now been completely fenced off," said Cizdyn.

Ockham will retain the full profit commissions from 1995 and 1995 for all its syndicates, and these will be paid in 1997 and 1998 due to the three-year accounting system at Lloyd's. The commissions for 1996 and onwards will be paid to the new owners.
"Lord Poole thinks that the wait for the Lloyd's profit commissions gives them the luxury of time to think what to go into next," said Cyzdin.
"But the stock market has a way of getting restless and it may end up kicking him into doing something," he said.
Ockham shareholders will be asked to approve the Ace and Questor transactions on Monday 25 November.
